candidates.summary: escapeGnoButtonTags runs after the bracket walker (line 385), so a link the walker spared stops parsing once the backslash goes in, and its bare brackets bind to the realm's own reference and footnote definitions
candidates.failure_scenario: User content `[a](<gno-button [evil]>)` goes through sanitize.Block or BlockRich. scanLinkURL (line 1195) accepts a pointy destination that contains a space, so the walker treats the span as an inline link and leaves `[a]` and the inner `[evil]` unescaped. escapeGnoButtonTags then rewrites it to `[a](\<gno-button [evil]>)`, a non-pointy destination with a space, which goldmark rejects. `[evil]` then becomes a shortcut reference to the realm chrome's `[evil]: https://realm.example/home` and renders as a link, and `[^evil]` binds the realm's footnote. The same holds for `[evil](<gno-button x>)` and for images. The unsanitized input binds to nothing. Running the sanitizer twice changes the output (`\[a\](\<gno-button \[evil\]>)`), which breaks the idempotence the native tests assert for every case.
